title: Using Claude to make the game, which game engine to export?
author: foohoa
selftext:
have been using claude to make the game until i think it was acceptable and it code with html java, would like to export to any game engine for better future update

Claude always recommend godot, but after export ot never success

so may i know you guys just using the html or export to other game engine?

comments.author: Technical-County-727
comments.body: You can’t export anything to godot. You have to program it either with gds or c# with mono version of godot

replies.author: foohoa
replies.body: Yes, was using web version, thanks for telling me as i have few hame idea always hit the wall in this step....

replies.author: Technical-County-727
replies.body: My suggestion would be to do some tutorials on godot so you learn the basics on how the scene system works and then bring in claude. Claude can work inside godot as the scene files are text, but it is quite clueless how things look or feel so you have to help with the basics some times.

replies.author: foohoa
replies.body: Thanks, will definitely looking for it and any game engine recommend? I will use godot is just claude recommend me, any other is ok for me

replies.author: Technical-County-727
replies.body: Godot for sure - I have done with unity, unreal and godot and at least I’ve had most fun with godot

replies.author: Technical-County-727
replies.body: So, download godot and visual code. Create a project with godot. Open the project folder with visual code. Install godot tools and claude extensions. Start chatting with claude in visual code and it will start working on your game.

comments.body: That ain't how it works champ

replies.body: That is how it works.  I ported like 10 cocos2dx using claude.

comments.body: I have had good success with Rust/Bevy that would be my choice for use with Claude Code.

replies.body: This look great, thanks for it

comments.body: I know nothing but I probably need it. And ways to use it with UE? I'm an artist and I can't handle nodes

comments.author: Happy-Fruit-8628
comments.body: If it’s already built with HTML and JavaScript, I’d just keep it web based. Moving it into something like Godot usually means rewriting a lot anyway. If it works, just keep improving what you have.

comments.author: AdditionalSteak9177
comments.body: I used a combination of all of them. The copilot in GitHub for the finishing touches…and pretty much all models are available in there.

comments.body: I use makermint studio for all my game dev work and it has been alright. Super easy to start and building games without a lot of technical knowledge

comments.body: cocos2dx is suprisingly easy for claude.
